title: Negotiation scorecard — contract allocations (working)
content:
Negotiation scorecard — per-contract allocation and fallback options (working doc)

Summary:
This sheet is a compact negotiation/ops scorecard to support commercial discussions for Dedicated capacity commitments. Focus: make counter-offer tradeoffs explicit (giveback windows, cushion, regional constraints, fallback model families) and capture operational risks that influence our offer.

Table: per-contract snapshot (live metrics are approximate, derived from billing + monitoring exports)

| Contract | Customer | Region | GPU SKU | Req (gpus) | Reserved (gpus) | Active avg util % | Oct committed | Nov planned | Dec planned | Cushion % | Risk |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| C-1209 | DataLens Inc | us-west-2 | H100-80GB | 160 | 120 | 72% | 120 | 120 | 120 | 12% | Medium: spikes for batch retraining; regional hot spot |
| C-1311 | Conversa.ai | eu-west-1 | A100-80GB | 48 | 64 | 55% | 48 | 56 | 56 | 25% | Low: can absorb burst to dedicated pool |
| C-1417 | HealthSyn | us-east-1 | H100-80GB | 200 | 200 | 88% | 200 | 200 | 200 | 6% | High: regulatory SLA; minimal tolerance for over-subscription |
| C-1498 | RetailMate | ap-southeast-1 | L40s | 40 | 24 | 38% | 24 | 32 | 40 | 65% | Medium: regional provisioning lead time 6–8 weeks |
| C-1503 | Searchly | global | Mixed (A100/H100) | 320 | 280 | 67% | 280 | 280 | 320 | 10% | Medium-high: cross-region routing required |

Calculated fields / quick notes:
- Cushion % = (Reserved - Req) / Req * 100 (positive means we hold extra capacity; negative would indicate shortfall).
- Active avg util % is 30-day rolling average of GPU occupancy for that contract's pods.
- Oct/Nov/Dec planned reflect negotiated phasing windows; columns are inputs for capacity runbook.

Suggested negotiation positions (ops + commercial):
- HealthSyn (C-1417): cannot reduce reserved; propose 9% reserved cushion for Z-score resiliency with option to increase commit for 6-month term at a 12% uplift on unit price. Flag SRE for a regional standby plan (us-east-1).
- DataLens (C-1209): propose a flexible burst buffer: keep 120 reserved, allow 40 transient burst credits capped to 20% of nightly traffic. Require 30-day notice to convert burst credits to permanent reservations.
- Conversa.ai (C-1311): they requested 48 -> we currently have 64 reserved. Recommend pro-rate discount for the first 3 months if they release 8 GPUs now, then re-evaluate after Nov traffic.
- RetailMate (C-1498): late APAC provisioning risk. Offer a staged ramp (24 -> 32 -> 40) tied to milestones in their implementation plan; include a 60-day contingency loan of GPUs from global spare pool if onboarding lags.

Operational constraints and fallbacks:
- Region-specific constraints: we have limited spare H100 capacity in eu-west-1 in Nov (estimated spare: 16 GPUs). If a customer upsizes, automatic fallback is to route traffic to us-west-2 with a cross-region latency SLA that they must accept (documented in the fallback policy).
- Model-family fallbacks: where acceptable, route to quantized A100 variants (A100-q8) for latency-sensitive low-cost paths; catalog these in routing policy RPG-019.
- Preemption and autoscale behavior: Dedicated nodes are non-preemptible; transient burst capacity will be delivered from 'burst-pool' (shared across contracts) and is preemptible with 2-hour notice.

Risk register (quick):
- High: HealthSyn (compliance exposure) -> require SOC2 attestation and KMS key separation (sales/legal already looped).
- Medium: APAC provisioning (hardware lead times) -> engineering to confirm order ETA by 2026-10-14.
- Low: Conversa.ai over-reservation -> resolved via pro-rate and 3-month reassessment.

Open questions (for pricing & legal):
- Standardize giveback window: 30-day vs 90-day? 30-day gives commercial flexibility but adds operational churn.
- Early-termination penalties: formula to recover amortized GPU procurement costs vs lost revenue.
- Cross-region routing acceptance: should we require explicit contract opt-in for fallback routing?

Action items (owners):
- Miguel: finalize fallback routing language and share with legal by 2026-10-08.
- Priya: confirm H100 spare pool numbers for eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 (due 2026-10-12).
- Evan: simulate 2-week burst scenario for Searchly to validate latency SLAs (due 2026-10-15).
- Sofia: prepare sales-facing counter-offer sheet with tiered pricing (due 2026-10-09).

Notes/history:
- This doc pulls from billing export (invoice-run 2026-09) + cluster-monitoring 30-day window. Keep as working; will convert to canonical allocation matrix if contracts sign.

Slack refs and tickets:
- See thread: #eng-infra (slack) thread: /thread/ENINF-contracts-alloc-2026-10 (internal)
- JIRA ENGINF-2147: "Dedicated reservation phasing engine" (linked above)

Versioning: draft v0.3 — negotiation pass 2.

---
Quick calc examples (copyable):
- Cushion % example (DataLens): (120 - 160) / 160 * 100 = -25% -> actually indicates shortfall; we show positive cushions only when reserved > requested. Fix: use absolute reserved vs requested view in sheet.
- Burst credit cost: unit_price * burst_hrs * GPUs * 1.25 uplift (premium for burst).

End of sheet (working).
